name: Jeiel
overview: Jeiel is a male member of the tribe of Levi, uniquely identified as the son of Mattaniah. His mention in Scripture is limited, with no additional notes provided to expand on his life or role. As a Levite, he would have been part of the priestly or temple service lineage.
namesAndTitles: The name Jeiel means 'G-d [El] has preserved,' reflecting a theologically rich meaning common in Hebrew names. This proper name is not indicated as being given directly by God but carries a significant reminder of divine preservation.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Jeiel as the son of Mattaniah. Additionally, it is inferred that Benaiah is his father, though this is not stated directly. Beyond these relationships, no further family connections are documented.
scriptureSignificance: Jeiel's significance in the biblical narrative rests primarily on his identification within the Levitical lineage as the son of Mattaniah. This connection situates him within the tribe entrusted with temple duties and worship, underscoring his role in the religious life of Israel. While details about his personal contributions are not provided, his inclusion highlights the importance of genealogical records in maintaining the priestly heritage.
